narrative.overview:
The site reads like a bulletin from the BBS era, typeset as a modern editorial page. Pages are indexes of a community's activity: events by year, projects by name, sedi, the board. Each entry gets a heavy sans headline and is separated from the next by a single hairline rule. Everything around the content is pure black, so the white type alone carries the page. Hierarchy comes from scale, weight and opacity, not from color, boxes or ornament.

Information is dense, but each line is easy to scan. Every piece of metadata (dates, places, breadcrumbs, emails, status) is set in IBM Plex Mono, and that mono voice is the system's link to its terminal heritage (`/home/metro/pescara`). Photographs show real people and the real lab. They sit in grayscale until hovered, then come back to color, the way a bulletin quotes reality rather than decorating with it.

The palette is monochrome by design. The only colors are status signals: red when a sede is closed, green when something is upcoming. Corners are square everywhere, and nothing casts a shadow.

The secondary north star is the discipline the bulletin is set in. From Swiss International Style it takes an objective grid that every element snaps to, flush-left ragged-right type, asymmetric balance instead of centered symmetry, strong contrast in scale between display and text, and photography used as fact, not mood. From the Bauhaus it takes form following function and an elementary geometry (square, circle, line) as the only source of graphic form. Where the two north stars meet, the bulletin decides *what* is said and Swiss/Bauhaus decides *how it is set*. When a choice is unclear, choose the one a Swiss typographer would defend on grid and legibility grounds.
keyCharacteristics: Pure black ground, white type at four fixed opacities, no decorative backgrounds.
IBM Plex Sans in the official MX hierarchy (H1 700, H2 600, H3 500), with Plex Mono reserved for machine text.
The official MX monogram in the nav; monogram + lettering in the footer.
Hairline rules (1px) and index-style rows instead of cards.
Square corners only. No shadows. Depth comes from tone and gradient overlays.
Grayscale photography that regains color on hover.
Color appears only as live status.
Swiss/Bauhaus discipline: grid-snapped, flush-left, asymmetric, elementary geometry.

rules.name: The LED Rule
rules.body: Red and green are status lights, not brand colors. They appear only where they report live state (open, closed, upcoming). Never use them for buttons, links, headings, highlights or campaign emphasis.

rules.name: The Four Whites Rule
rules.body: Text uses exactly four values: 100%, 80%, 62% and 46% white. The lowest tier is set so that every tier passes WCAG AA (4.5:1) on black. Hierarchy is decided by choosing among them. Don't introduce a fifth opacity or a tinted gray.

rules.name: The No Bauhaus Primaries Rule
rules.body: The Bauhaus influence is formal (geometry, function), not chromatic. Red/yellow/blue primaries are not adopted. Color stays governed by The LED Rule.

rules.name: The Machine Text Rule
rules.body: Plex Mono is only for text a machine would produce or read: paths, URLs, domains, emails, handles, IDs, code, and dates aligned in a column. Navigation, buttons, labels and sentences are Plex Sans. Mono is Regular only.

rules.name: The Manual Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Heading weights follow the MX manual: H1 Bold 700, H2 SemiBold 600, H3 Medium 500, emphasis SemiBold 600. Nothing is heavier than 700.

rules.name: The Flush Left Rule
rules.body: All type is set flush-left, ragged-right. No centered headings, no justified text. Contrast comes from the jump in scale between display and body (about 4:1), not from intermediate sizes.

rules.name: The Objective Grid Rule
rules.body: Every element aligns to the column and to the 12-column grid the mosaic already uses. Elements that break out of the column (like the full-bleed mosaic) do so on the grid, never on an arbitrary offset.

rules.name: The Asymmetry Rule
rules.body: Composition balances by weight, not by mirroring: a heavy title against open space, a narrow label column against a wide content column (as in the event and project rows). Avoid centered, symmetric layouts.

rules.name: The No Lift Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. Hover feedback is a tone fill, a color step to white, or a small horizontal nudge (4–16px). It is never a shadow or a vertical lift.

rules.name: The Elementary Forms Rule
rules.body: All graphic form comes from Bauhaus primitives: the square, the circle and the line. Use them in white or white tiers, built from geometry (CSS or SVG). Each project has a 24px outline mark (1.5px stroke, square caps) built from these primitives: a node triangle (Abruzzo Off-Grid), a struck-through square (Stop Piracy-Shield), a circle around a square (Refurbish Ninja), a tent of lines (MOCA), and broadcast arcs (CYBER-FREEDOM). The 7px status dot is the existing circle.

dos: Do keep the page ground true black (#000) and draw all structure with 1px #1a1a1a hairlines.
Do set every date, place, path, email and status in Plex Mono, and every name and sentence in Plex Sans.
Do build lists as hairline-separated index rows with the tone-fill and nudge hover.
Do show photography in grayscale at rest and bring back color only on hover.
Do use the CTA Line for primary navigation-style calls to action.
Do use the expo-out ease `cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)` for movement and 0.2s linear color transitions for hover color changes.
Do set all type flush-left and snap every element to the column grid.
Do build icons and graphic marks from squares, circles and lines.
donts: Don't redraw, recolour, stretch or annotate the MX logo, or typeset "metro olografix" beside it. Use the official SVGs.
Don't use Plex Mono for navigation, buttons or sentences, or at any weight other than Regular.
Don't use red or green for anything except live status (The LED Rule).
Don't round corners or add box-shadows to any surface.
Don't introduce a text opacity outside 100/80/62/46%.
Don't use Unicode glyphs (`((•))`, `◇`, `↻`, `⌘`, `☆`) as project or feature icons. They are slated for replacement and should not be extended into new work.
Don't wrap content in filled cards. Rows and hairline lattices carry the structure.
Don't center or justify text, and don't bring in Bauhaus red/yellow/blue.
